species: mouse (SOD1 G93A transgenic, B6SJL background; wild-type littermates)
readout_other: rotarod; grip strength; open field; shear wave elastography of gastrocnemius; H&E/GAF muscle staining; Nissl; c-Fos and microglia immunofluorescence; onset and lifespan
direction_notes: Motor cortex LIPUS increased c-Fos-positive cells (about 240% of sham) in WT mice; in SOD1 G93A mice it delayed disease onset (10.7%), extended lifespan (6.7%) and improved motor performance.
safety_notes: H&E and Nissl staining showed no damage or hemorrhage in the motor cortex after 30-min LIPUS.

timing.protocol_description: PRF 100 Hz, duty cycle 10%, stimulation time 6 s, tone-burst length 1 ms; 20 min per session every other day, three sessions per week for four weeks.

source_quotes.n_subjects: The above mice were randomly allocated into three groups: WT-sham (WT, $n = 1 2 )$ , sham–LIPUS + TG (sham–LIPUS, $n = 1 6 )$ , and LIPUS + TG (LIPUS, n = 16).
